subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a first-class durable conversational rule-governance layer and cross-channel explicit multi-bot mention semantics, or keep this as memory-plugin/channel-plugin/API design work?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses memory authority, durable storage, workspace file precedence, conflict handling, and channel delivery policy, and current code has useful pieces but no settled product contract.

options.title: Design contract first
options.body: Keep this open as a maintainer-sponsored design tracker that defines rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and mention semantics before implementation.

options.title: Split narrow fixes
options.body: Track Feishu self-mention loss and channel-specific delivery bugs separately, and only reopen durable rule learning when maintainers want that product direction.

options.title: Route through plugin/API path
options.body: Require the durable rule-learning capability to prove it cannot be built through memory or channel plugin APIs before adding core rule-layer surface.

recommendation.title: Design contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this open as a maintainer-sponsored design tracker that defines rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and mention semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent cross-surface history across the inspected memory, prompt/context, and Feishu runtime boundaries.
